content.text:
Resubmitted.

**Repair made in operative language:** new Section 7.7 now expressly designates our side as the **"Customer"** — "The Issuer (the "Customer" for the Servicer's services) may terminate this Agreement ... for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer, in which case the Servicer will refund **to the Customer** pro rata any fees prepaid for the period after the effective date of the termination." The alias is both defined and used in the same clause, so the convenience right is expressed in Customer-named operative text with no undefined term or dangling reference.

**Otherwise unchanged and deliberate:**
- Preferred level retained — the fallback would concede a Servicer term-end convenience exit on 90 days' notice that Section 7.1 currently forbids.
- Element 4 mapped `already_met` on retained Section 7.1's no-resignation bar; not restated in any operation.
- Only one other edit: the Section 8.3 "earlier" → "earliest to occur of a termination under Section 7.7," conforming change, so the natural-expiry formula does not contradict the new exit. Clauses (a) and (b) are preserved verbatim; I left them unlettered-first rather than relettering, since the verifier confirmed the provision is operative as written and relettering would add churn for tidiness only.
- No "in whole or in part", no survival tail, expense allocation, or procedural extras. Sections 7.2(c), 7.3, 7.4 and 7.6 are untouched.
